STARTERPhonics · Lesson 1
A–Z

The English Alphabet

English has 26 letters and about 40 sounds. This lesson shows how they work.

Introduction

126 letters

Aa Bb Cc Dd Ee Ff Gg Hh Ii Jj Kk Ll Mm Nn Oo Pp Qq Rr Ss Tt Uu Vv Ww Xx Yy Zz
Vowels (5): A  E  I  O  U Consonants (21): all the other letters

Y is a consonant, but sometimes it sounds like a vowel.  my · happy

2A letter has a name and a sound

We say the name when we spell a word. We say the sound when we read.

B Name/biː/ Sound/b/ As inbag
M Name/em/ Sound/m/ As inmap
S Name/es/ Sound/s/ As insun

3More sounds than letters

English has 26 letters but about 40 sounds. So one letter can have more than one sound, and two letters can work together to make one sound. You will learn them step by step.

4Sound symbols

A sound symbol shows how we say a sound, not how we write it. We write it between two lines.

/æ/the sound of A in cat
/iː/the mark ː means a long sound

5How to read this book

catOrange letters are the letters we are learning.
makeGrey letters are silent. We do not say them.
ALWAYSThe rule never changes.
USUALLY TRUEThe rule has a few exceptions.
NOT FIXED — LEARN EACH WORDThere is no rule. Learn each word.

Aa

The Letter A

A is the first letter of the alphabet. It is a vowel with four main sounds.

Vowel4 sounds

1The sounds of A

/æ/
Short A
  • cat
  • map
  • bag
/eɪ/
Long A — it says its name
  • baby
  • paper
  • radio
/ɑː/
Open A — open your mouth
  • want
  • wash
  • pasta
/ə/
Weak A — a soft, short sound
  • about
  • again
  • sofa

2When is A silent?

A is almost never silent on its own.

Ee

The Letter E

E is the most common letter in English. It has three main sounds.

Vowel3 sounds

1The sounds of E

/e/
Short E
  • bed
  • pen
  • ten
/iː/
Long E — it says its name
  • me
  • we
  • even
/ə/
Weak E — a soft, short sound
  • open
  • problem
  • moment

2When is E silent?

At the end of a word, E is usually silent.
It often helps the vowel before it say its name.

makehometime
Grey letter = silent
USUALLY TRUE

Short words with only one vowel say the E:
me · we · be

3E with other letters

ee
/iː/seetreegreen
ALMOST ALWAYS
ea
/iː/teaseaeat
/e/breadhead
NOT FIXED — LEARN EACH WORD

The Letter I

I is a vowel. It has four main sounds.

Vowel4 sounds

1The sounds of I

/ɪ/
Short I

  • big
/aɪ/
Long I — it says its name
  • hi
  • kind
  • tiger
/iː/
Like long E — in words from other languages

  • pizza
  • visa
/ə/
Weak I — a soft, short sound

2When is I silent?

I is almost never silent on its own.

/eɪ/rainwaitpaint

Oo

The Letter O

O is a vowel. It has five main sounds.

Vowel5 sounds

1The sounds of O

/ɑː/
Short O — American English
  • hot
  • box
  • stop
/oʊ/
Long O — it says its name
  • go
  • no
  • hotel
/ʌ/
Like the U in "cup"
  • money
  • month
  • front
/uː/
A long "oo" sound
  • do
  • to
  • into
/ə/
Weak O — a soft, short sound
  • today
  • lemon
  • second

2When is O silent?

O is silent in a few words.

peopleleopard
Grey letter = silent
NOT A RULE — A FEW WORDS

3O with other letters

oa
/oʊ/boatcoatroad
ALMOST ALWAYS
oi
/ɔɪ/oilcoinboil
ALMOST ALWAYS
oo
/uː/foodmoontoo
/ʊ/bookgoodlook

Uu

The Letter U

U is the last of the five vowels. It has five main sounds.

Vowel5 sounds

1The sounds of U

/ʌ/
Short U
  • cup
  • bus
  • sun
/juː/
Long U — it says its name
  • music
  • menu
  • unit
/uː/
A long "oo" sound
  • flu
  • super
  • truth
/ʊ/
A short "oo" sound
  • put
  • push
  • full
/ə/
Weak U — a soft, short sound
  • focus
  • minus
  • album

2When is U silent?

U is almost never silent on its own.

3U with other letters

au
/ɑː/Augustauthorlaundry
A few words are different: laugh

ou

/ʌ/countryyoungtouch
